aim: Determine whether independent within-species observations across AusTraits source datasets are numerous enough to calibrate trait-specific observational noise independently of the previously observed K ranking.

record_definition.join: Exact source-native K family and trait and species-rank taxon; numeric finite values in original source trait-config units, deduplicated by (dataset_id,observation_id,value), with one genus per species; no observed-K-dependent filtering.
record_definition.species_state: Use the original matched median of numeric observations for the K trait-state eligibility check; for log-scale repeatability, positive records only.
record_definition.independent_observation: Distinct dataset_id + observation_id record key, not two identical rows.
record_definition.independent_dataset: Distinct nonempty dataset_id; at least 2 datasets for the same family+trait+species.
record_definition.meaning: Across-dataset dispersion measures observational/intraspecific/source heterogeneity; it is not a pure instrument measurement-error estimate.

predeclared_feasibility.decision: Proceed to source-calibrated error-process null only if at least 6 of 13 traits each have at least 30 multidataset species from at least 3 families with 5 or more such species; otherwise report that independent calibration is not sufficiently supported for this 13-trait graph.

inference_firewall: Run no new K association/regression against source-repeatability descriptors during feasibility.
Do not tune noise intensities from observed K, family ICC, rank gain, pair reversal or OU discrepancy.
Do not label source heterogeneity as instrument measurement error.
Never treat duplicate records from one dataset or observation_id as independent replicates.
Keep original prospective rho replication failure, Brownian and OU outcomes unchanged.
Descriptive source coverage is an exploratory post-K/OU workflow, not independent preregistration of the original discovery.
